explanation: Luggage may only go on the passenger deck at the driver's discretion and must be placed where it will not obstruct the aisle or emergency exits, since keeping clear passage for riders takes priority over cargo convenience.
A driver may refuse a child's trolley only when the bus is genuinely crowded and there is no safe space left for it, balancing accessibility against not endangering other standing passengers.
A reverse buzzer that sounds automatically whenever reverse gear is engaged is a mandatory safety feature, warning pedestrians and other road users who may be in the bus's large rear blind spot.

The pictured marker is the kilometer-post sign, which states the cumulative distance travelled along that route, unlike signs that color-code route classification or plates that announce distance to an upcoming hazard.

A school bus must carry special flashing lights at front and back that activate specifically when the doors open, warning approaching traffic exactly at the moment children may be boarding or stepping into the road.

A bus left standing at night on an inter-urban road must be marked with a warning triangle visible from at least 100 meters and with its hazard flashers running, since approaching vehicles need early warning at highway speeds.

Bus interior lights must be on during 'lighting-up time,' the same legally defined period that governs when a vehicle's exterior lights must be lit, so passengers can see to move safely inside the cabin in low light.

The bus driver personally bears responsibility for keeping the passenger cabin clean, as part of the driver's general duty of care over the vehicle they operate, rather than delegating it to the owner or dispatcher.

Smoking on a bus is banned outright under the law against smoking in enclosed public places, and operators must additionally post a visible 'no smoking' notice so passengers are clearly informed of the rule.

Only paraplegic (wheelchair) tag holders are granted the specific legal exemption to use a bus lane, since this stricter mobility-tag category is what the regulation names, not disabled tags in general.
The bus-lane privilege attaches to the disabled person's vehicle and tag rather than requiring them to be the one driving, so an authorized escort driving on their behalf may still use the lane.

Passengers are legally required to follow the instructions of on-duty bus service employees, since obeying staff directions is part of maintaining order and safety for everyone aboard public transport.

A bus driver must remain on board at the final stop until every passenger has disembarked, since ending the shift early could strand passengers or leave them without proper supervision while alighting.
A panoramic mirror is mounted at the front of the bus, angled back toward the cabin, so the driver can monitor all passengers and passenger behavior without having to turn around while driving.
Explosives and other inflammable materials are never permitted on a bus, since even small quantities pose a fire or explosion risk to every passenger confined in the enclosed vehicle.

A 'school-children transport vehicle' is defined by its dedicated purpose, a private bus or public vehicle specifically used to carry school children, rather than by simply being any bus or any vehicle that happens to carry them.

Lost property found on public vehicles must be handed to the police or dealt with according to prior arrangements with the route service owner, so drivers do not personally decide who gets the item back.
Letting passengers off on a freeway is prohibited outright, since freeways ban pedestrian presence entirely and the high speeds make any roadside disembarkation extremely dangerous.
The pictured sign warns that a tunnel is coming up ahead, telling drivers to prepare for reduced light and width by adjusting their speed and lights before entering.

'Student transport' specifically means carrying students to school or an organized school activity outside the framework of a regular scheduled route service, which is why it carries its own extra safety rules for doors and supervision.
A taxi must have wastebaskets placed both beside the driver's seat and beside the back seat, giving passengers convenient access at both ends of the cabin to keep the vehicle clean.
The taxi roof-sign must show 'available' whenever there are no passengers in the vehicle, since the sign is meant to reflect real-time occupancy status rather than the time of day or season.

Both the vehicle owner and the driver share responsibility for displaying the route map, briefing, and fare list as instructed by the Controller of Road Transport, so passengers always have access to accurate official information.

A route-service bus may only stop at the stations approved by the Controller of Road Transport as part of its route license, ensuring predictable, safe stopping points rather than anywhere a passenger requests.

A vehicle's license category sets its own legal passenger cap independent of the physical minibus's separate capacity, so a Class B license limits carriage to eight passengers excluding the driver regardless of how many seats the vehicle has.

Only a person or business certified by the Authority as an authorized service provider may repair or set a taxi meter, a control meant to prevent tampering with the device that determines what passengers are charged.
On urban roads a taxi may stop to board or drop passengers anywhere parking is allowed, including beside red-white curbstones, as long as doing so does not disturb the flow of traffic.
Sightseeing or touring rides require the taxi driver to hold a specific permit from the Ministry of Tourism, an added certification beyond the standard taxi license needed to serve tourists properly.

On non-urban roads, the seats reserved for security personnel are the two front seats on either side of the aisle, giving them the clearest sightlines and quickest response position on intercity routes.
The law sets a fixed maximum length of 13.5 meters for a standard dual-axle bus, a limit chosen to keep such vehicles maneuverable and safe on the road.

Packages may be carried on a bus only if they do not disturb or endanger the passengers, reflecting the general principle that passenger safety and comfort take priority over freight convenience on a passenger vehicle.
A bus is treated as a public place under the smoking-prohibition law regardless of how many passengers it is carrying, since the health risk from smoke exposure applies whenever anyone is aboard.

A speed retarder is mandatory on buses with a minimum all-up weight of 10,000 kg, since heavier buses need extra braking assistance to control their greater momentum on descents without overheating the brakes.
A taxi roof-sign is an illuminated device mounted on the roof used for identification purposes, distinct from the meter box or any recording device inside the vehicle.
Driving a bus with a door open is forbidden outright, since an open door while moving risks passengers or objects falling out or being struck by nearby traffic.

Marking certain bus seats as reserved for people with disabilities is a courtesy designation rather than an enforceable legal duty, so a passenger is not obliged to vacate a seat that was already assigned in advance.

The pictured warning sign shows a downhill grade with a distance plate stating how far ahead the hazard begins, so it reads as an advance warning of a steep descent starting about 2,500 meters further on, not one already underway or ending.

A 'bus' is legally defined as a motor vehicle built to carry at least eight passengers besides the driver and formally listed as a bus in its registration document, not merely any vehicle used to move people.
A taxi driver may not smoke while driving, since the same enclosed-public-place smoking ban that protects bus passengers applies equally to taxis, regardless of passenger consent or ventilation.

When passengers start fighting, a bus driver should head toward the nearest police station or seek out a policeman en route, since involving law enforcement is safer than physically intervening or ignoring the conflict while driving.

A rescue kit is required specifically on touring vehicles and buses running inter-urban route service lines, since these longer-distance routes carry a greater risk of being far from immediate emergency help.
Because changing the size of drive-system parts alters the mechanical basis the meter uses to calculate fare, the taxi meter must be recalibrated within forty-eight hours to keep charges accurate.

Buses specifically must keep their interior lights on during 'lighting-up time,' since passengers need to see the aisle and seats safely at night, a requirement that does not extend the same way to taxis or other hired vehicles.
A bus driver is never permitted to smoke while driving, without exception for touring rides or passenger consent, since it remains an enclosed vehicle used to carry the public.

A passenger who fails to show a ticket when asked must pay the bus fare plus a fine set according to the type of ride, since fare evasion carries both restitution and a penalty rather than just a warning.

The driver or conductor may refuse boarding to someone wearing skiing or skating boots because such footwear is a genuine safety hazard on a moving bus, unlike traveling one stop, paying with a large note, or bringing a properly contained animal.

Special taxis may run share-taxi rides only through a corporation holding a license for that specific route and with the corporation's written approval, since shared fixed-route service requires proper route licensing rather than ad hoc arrangement.

No fee may be charged for carrying a wheelchair on a taxi, protecting disabled passengers from extra cost, though the driver is still allowed to decline carrying more than one wheelchair for practical space reasons.

Operating a taxi at Ben-Gurion Airport requires a specific permit from the Licensing Authority and strict adherence to that permit's terms, including where the taxi may stop and park, since airport traffic needs tighter control than ordinary street hailing.

The Authority may suspend a taxi license when the license holder fails to appear after being properly summoned, an administrative enforcement tool that exists separately from a court's power to suspend a license.
A bus driver may permit luggage on board only on condition that it does not disturb or endanger the other passengers, since passenger safety and comfort outrank the convenience of carrying freight.
The regulations governing bus passenger conduct and safety apply equally to taxi passengers, since both are riders of public transport vehicles under the same legal framework.

The Minister of Transport sets the taxi fare through a special order under the Control of Prices of Commodities and Services framework, since taxi pricing is treated as a nationally regulated price rather than one set by drivers or associations.
The fare for a special taxi ride is likewise determined by the Minister of Transport, keeping fare-setting centralized rather than left to individual companies or the taxi association.
Share taxi rides taken between 23:31 and 04:59 carry a fixed 25 percent night surcharge, compensating for the reduced demand and higher operating burden of the late-night hours.
Only the Controller of Road Transport authorizes and processes a change of ownership for a taxi license, ensuring that regulatory oversight follows the license even when it changes hands.

The pictured sign still permits a taxi to briefly stop, load, or unload passengers on an urban road provided doing so does not disturb traffic, since the restriction is not an absolute ban in that setting.

The pictured sign bars a driving-instruction bus from entering, because the vehicle remains classified and registered as a bus, and the restriction targets that vehicle category regardless of the trip's instructional purpose.
The pictured sign's terms for buses apply based on the vehicle's classification, so a bus without passengers still counts as a bus and may enter according to what the sign provides.
A taxi remains a taxi under the pictured sign's terms even without passengers aboard, so it may enter on an urban road as long as it causes no obstruction to traffic.
Since a public minibus meets the legal definition of a bus, it is entitled to the same access the pictured sign grants to buses, provided it satisfies the sign's stated conditions.

The pictured sign marks a spot where public-vehicle passengers may be loaded and unloaded without the vehicle being required to wait there afterward, distinguishing quick drop-off from a waiting area.
The pictured sign designates the location exclusively for taxi passenger loading and unloading, so any other type of vehicle is barred from using that spot to pick up or drop off riders.
The pictured sign marks a no-parking zone that applies to every vehicle category, including taxis, without any day-of-week or time-based exception.
The pictured no-parking sign applies to a minibus the same way it applies to any other vehicle, since the restriction is based on the location, not on the specific vehicle type.
The pictured no-parking restriction covers a public minibus regardless of its 3,300 kg weight, since the sign's prohibition is not limited only to the heaviest weight class of vehicles.

The pictured no-parking sign likewise bars a private minibus weighing 2,700 kg, since the restriction applies to the parking location generally rather than being conditioned on a specific weight threshold.
The pictured no-parking sign also prohibits a 4,500 kg bus from parking there, confirming the restriction is a general one that is not limited to only the very heaviest vehicles.
A licensed taxi may use a designated bus lane even without passengers aboard, since the lane privilege is granted to that class of public-service vehicle rather than depending on current occupancy.

A public minibus may use the designated bus lane even without passengers, since it qualifies as a public-transport vehicle under the sign's terms regardless of whether it is currently carrying anyone.
A taxi carrying passengers is clearly within the class of vehicles the sign permits to use a designated bus lane, since licensed taxis are among the vehicles authorized for that lane.

A private minibus that meets the vehicle category the sign permits may use the designated bus lane even without passengers aboard, since the privilege attaches to the vehicle's classification rather than its current occupancy.
Before entering service, a bus driver is legally required to carry out both a security check and a safety check of the vehicle, going beyond merely cleaning mirrors or windshields.
Before moving the bus, a driver must check for road users hiding in the blind spots, since the general duty of care requires being aware of everything near the vehicle before setting it in motion.
After passengers board and before pulling away, a bus driver must confirm that the doors are closed, since starting to move with an open door risks a passenger falling or being struck.

The pictured sign marks the end of the restriction that bars vehicles over 10,000 kg from parking, so past that point a heavy vehicle may park at night, unlike the other signs which actively prohibit it.
Sudden braking risks throwing standing or unsecured bus passengers forward and injuring them, which is why gradual, anticipated braking is stressed as the safer practice for a bus driver.

The pictured sign is the triangular warning marker that alerts drivers to an approaching tunnel, prompting them to prepare their speed and lights before entering, unlike the sign marking the tunnel's end.
The law requires the rear of a semi-trailer forming part of an articulated vehicle to carry warning stickers, alerting following drivers to the extended, jointed shape of the vehicle ahead.

Student transport requires picking up and dropping off pupils only through the front right door, keeping a single supervised boarding point under the driver's direct view rather than allowing multiple entry points.

In a student transport minibus, boarding and dropping off happens through the front right door or another door located at the vehicle's front, preserving the same principle of supervised, front-of-vehicle access.
Driving students while they are standing is prohibited, since every child must be seated to avoid injury from sudden braking, turning, or other normal driving movements.

A warning triangle must be carried by all motor vehicles, including trailers and semi-trailers, but not motorcycles, reflecting the standard breakdown-warning equipment rule that exempts two-wheelers.

When driving near a group of children, a driver must slow down and be ready to stop completely if needed, since children can behave unpredictably and dart into the road without warning, as the general duty of care requires.

The combination of a blue light with a flashing yellow light is reserved specifically for integrated policing vehicles, distinguishing that vehicle category from ambulances, fire trucks, or rescue vehicles which use different signal combinations.
A fire extinguisher must be placed somewhere visible with easy access so it can be used quickly in an emergency, rather than being locked away or stored somewhere impractical like the roof.

Economic fuel consumption comes from shifting into the appropriate gear and keeping a moderate speed up to about 90 km/h, since most vehicles reach their best fuel efficiency in that range and correct gearing avoids wasteful engine revving.

Fuel consumption is reduced by driving calmly within the speed limit and keeping tire pressure correct, since under-inflated tires increase rolling resistance and aggressive driving wastes fuel through unnecessary acceleration and braking.
Following the manufacturer's regular maintenance schedule reduces both fuel consumption and the wear and tear on vehicle parts, keeping the engine and components running at their intended efficiency.
Manual transmission vehicles typically consume less fuel than automatics, since the driver can select the optimal gear directly rather than relying on the automatic system's broader shifting logic.

A driver's ability to control the vehicle and avoid accidents is greater the slower they drive, since lower speed shortens both reaction distance and braking distance, shrinking the zone in which the driver has no control at all.
On an oily road section, a driver should slow down as gently as possible and avoid heavy braking, since oil sharply reduces tire grip and hard braking on that low-friction surface risks a skid.
On a road with bumps and cracks, a driver must slow down and adjust speed to the road's condition, since the general duty of care requires driving at a speed the surface can actually support safely.

A policeman may stop a vehicle and have it checked specifically because of the level of pollution emitted from its engine, since excess emissions are one of the defined legal grounds for such a roadside check.

A policeman may issue a vehicle non-use notice when the vehicle causes air pollution beyond the permitted levels, since excessive pollution is one of the specific statutory grounds for taking a vehicle off the road immediately.

It is advised to turn lights on during the day when the sun is behind the driver, since oncoming drivers facing into that low sun may struggle to see a dark vehicle silhouetted against the bright sky, and headlights make it more visible to them.

When a vehicle suddenly emerges into your lane from the opposite direction, the safest response is to slow down and pull as far right as possible, even onto the hard shoulder if necessary, rather than swerving into the opposing lane or relying on horn and high beam to fix the situation.
Headlights that are not properly adjusted fail to illuminate the road the way the law requires, which can leave hazards under-lit or, if aimed too high, blind oncoming drivers instead.

Commercial vehicles with an all-up weight over 15,000 kg are permitted freight up to 3.40 meters wide when it is carried as a single indivisible unit, a wider allowance than lighter vehicle classes receive.

A police authorization becomes obligatory for transporting long freight once the combined length of the vehicle and its load exceeds 20 meters, since an oversized combination that long needs escort to manage the added traffic risk.
